newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends mostly higher, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends mostly higher, trade thin.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended the year with modest gains Tuesday in trade thinned by Wednesday's New Year holiday, market sources said.
"This market is dead in the water," said one dealer.
Traders said stronger natural gas futures lent some support to a power market undermined recently by wet, warm weather in much of the western U.S.
They also noted that February contracts have fallen sharply over the past two weeks, indicating some technical support at recent levels.
But the power futures complex, which was launched by NYMEX at the end of March, still "doesn't do technicals very well," said one trader.

He and others said abundant hydroelectric power in the Pacific Northwest and Northern California has put a damper on the market, although this could change if the weather turns cold and river flows slow down.
February 1997 COB futures closed 41 cents higher at $14.61 per megawatt hour (MWh), while the March contract was up 40 cents at $13.40. Other COB contracts settled 10 cents lower to 45 cents higher.
February Palo Verde was up 52 cents at $15.80, while March was 40 cents higher at $15.10. Other PV contracts ended 10 cents higher to 75 cents lower.
As of 1250 EST, 42 COB and 15 PV contracts were sold.
